title: Amazing App, Lots of Potential, A Few Suggestions
body:
Super cool app. Love the design and simplicity. Keeps me motivated. It is reasonable with what is free and what cost money. They don’t try to scam!! Love love LOVE that there’s no longer a limit on how many tasks I can do at once. Love the other pages as well, super helpful! Some ideas I thought would be fun and thought the creators might think so too:

-A friend system that you can add each other and see each others progress/remind them to complete tasks.(would help promote the app by encouraging people to share it)

-The ability to delete tags, I like to organize everything (if you already can, I can’t find it lol)

-More health tasks in the top as well as water (protein intake, carbs, steps), would love to see all of my goals in one app to keep me on track lol

-More colours for tasks (maybe a colour wheel so people can make their own)/making cute themes available for tasks so it can be more aesthetic 

-More emojis for tasks (there’s a lot of food and not a lot of cleaning symbols lol)

-An upgrade to the tag system so habits are more differentiated and organized. Like the heath tasks bar. Could make a morning routine, night routine, daily cleaning routine etc 
+
An area to quickly and simply write things that only need to be done that day or within the week, similar to a To-Do list. Like as if separating the current system into long-term (routines that are planned ahead and repeated regularly) and short-term (one time tasks that need to be completed that day or within the week) instead of having it all in one spot

-The ability to swipe from page to page instead of clicking on the icons (would encourage more use)

-An earning system. Every task or routine a person completes, they get exp and/or coins. The exp can go towards a level system that increases with exp and the coins can be used to temporarily buy premium perks (again, encouraging more use/giving customers a better idea on the perks of premium aka encouraging more people to buy)

-An upgrade to the widget bar that will show what tasks need to be done in that moment instead of in general, as well as replacing the tasks that are completed with ones incompleted

-Maybe an option for something similar to the Apple calendar format where you visually see where you blocked out specific times for which task or routine


Sorry for the whole essay but I see a lot of potential in this app. As a person with ADHD, these suggestions are things that I find make apps highly addictive and encourage me to use them consistently. And if any app should be addictive, it should be the ones that benefit you such as Me+🩷✨

title: Beware No “FREE” trial
body: I was looking into Me+ and wanted a one month subscription. Then a one year subscription with a “one week free trial” was offered at a good price, so I chose that option. Within the hour, I changed my mind and went to cancel my new subscription, as one can do with any “free trial”. I was only able to cancel the renewal in a year, my card had already been charged and there is no way to cancel or get a refund. I have emailed back and forth several times, with Me+ only being interested in keeping my money. That have not addressed or acknowledged the false advertising of a “free trial”. They have offered me all kinds of discounts and perks to keep this subscription. At this point it’s just the principle of it. I believe my email conversations have been with IA, auto responses or robots and not real humans which has also been not productive and frustrating. Finally they said they wanted to help me process a refund and asked for my receipts, but then they stopped responding. I think it’s a neat concept and app to be fair, but offering a free trial and then charging your card with no option for refund is unethical and needs to be fixed. Do better!!

title: I LOVE THIS APP… with a few exceptions
body:
I’ve always used a paper schedular for everything… but it’s not something I carried around all the time. This app is great for that! 

I love the mood check in, the journal entries, the ability to schedule notifications for certain things and the little bursts of motivation and applause for getting things done. I filled out a survey and it said I was at risk for severe depression (which I know) but the app offered to get me in touch with a therapist. How incredible is that?

And the widget so you can see your list whenever you go on your phone? AMAZING!

However… I cannot justify $75 a year or $13 a month. If it was $50 or under for the year, I would purchase in a heart beat. I think they should offer options as I won’t utilize the entire app (such as the videos and such) they should offer a cheaper version with less features.

Also, a huge negative was that you can’t just take something on your list and move it over to the next day. You also can’t check off things you put on your list for future dates which is crummy because if you happen to get something done early it’s nice to be able to check it off. I’m not sure why that’s not an option? 

Anyways, great app. A bit too pricey for me and I assume for the majority of people this app would be great for - students.

title: Love it! Easy and fun to use. Also helps with ADHD
body:
(Disclaimer: English isn’t my first language)

It is so easy and fun to write down the tasks. The app is very colourful and you can choose different colours for different tasks. The app has a variety of colours that you can choose from. When you write the task, there’s also an emoji at the top. There is a variety of emoji’s you can choose from. As a younger person with ADHD, this app helps me do many productive things during the day. Since I have a different schedule for different days, having separate schedules for each day in the app helps me be less confused on which alarms are for today, contrary to when I use the app that comes with the iPhone. (When I use the one in iPhone I do get confused). I would extremely recommend this app to anyone that has ADHD or a similar situation, and anyone in general that relates to what I said about getting confused with the alarms.

title: Paid for the year for a glorified checklist? (False Advertisement)
body:
When I first downloaded the app, it was quite helpful when it suggested stretches for my morning routine. It appeared to be more helpful than it actually was. Now that I’ve been using it for a few days, I’m realizing that this is just a checklist with reminders. The explore page is overwhelmingly bland and unappealing, the daily checklists and reminders you can totally just do on your phone. The appeal of this app is that it helps you with these tasks but instead it just gives you the task and advertises its other apps every other time you check off a task. Before you ask, yes, I have the JustFit app as well, the issue is there’s no search option for both and I find myself scrolling for things that should be easy to find: Stretches, more disability inclusive workouts.

I digress, this specific app clutters itself up. If you have ADHD like me and get overwhelmed quick by disorganized lists(because the way they do organize the tasks like morning routines and healthy lifestyle is NOT helpful) than please just sit down with yourself and create your own list(maybe off pinterest for inspo) and DON’T pay for this app! Create a plan that works for you, that catches your own attention, and don’t rely on this app to get you far on habit building.

Don’t pay for this service, it’s exploiting people with ADHD, people with burnout, and first time mothers. It’s ripping you off when you’re already trying to help yourself and you don’t deserve that 🩵

If anyone reads this, take care, and I hope you find something that works for you.

title: Instant charge up-front disguised as free trial
body:
This is a cute app and I would like it, but as others have commented, selecting a free trial will just instantly charge you for $18.99, as opposed to charging you when the “trial period” ends like most free-trial apps. It charges you upfront meaning you have to take up any complaints / payment corrections with your credit card company or Apple, which is a huge hassle.

If they turned off the instant payment and honoured an actual 7-day free trial before issuing payment, it would give users a chance to try it (or cancel it) without being annoyed. 

It’s a shame because it’s a cute app and I like it, but it feels scammy to charge up front when its advertised as a free trial.

I decided to just buy premium because $25/year wasn’t too bad. I love that I can colour code tasks, as well as add my own and customize tasks. But I do wish I could add tasks for just one day, and not have that repeat. As well as to be able to delete one task, especially a repeating task for one day if something comes up and changes my plans for the day, and not have that impact anything else or for other days.

My work schedule is unfortunately very inconsistent for days worked and days off. My days off are never the same for each week and that makes it hard for me, someone who needs predictable stability, to form consistent patterns and habits, which is why I downloaded and purchased this app. But finding out I can’t set my chores and tasks for my one day off and not have that repeat for each following day is a little disappointing and makes me feel less inclined to use this app. 

I did pay for the year so I will mess around with this app more and become more familiar with it as it’s just been a few days since I’ve had this app. But I do wish I could add/remove tasks for just one day without it repeating. I hope y’all implement a feature for that in the near future. 🖤💙💚

title: Good but needs work
body: Had the free trial been a bit longer than seven days, I wouldn’t have purchased. I feel like with some development tweaks this app could be amazing. For instance, it always defaults to the first day you started the app when you go to check your sleep sounds. So you always have to go to the drop-down menu to the current date. In the feed where it shows daily information, it cuts off. For instance for horoscope, it will display two sentences and then you can tell there was more but there’s no way to expand. I wish there was an option to have a gradual alarm, instead of a blast right from the start. I’ve since turned the alarm off and just use my iPad. Finally, I am not seeing the same features that are advertised through Instagram on this actual app. There’s supposed to be a way to prioritize my routine based on Myers Briggs? Again, I wouldn’t have paid the yearly subscription had I had a bit longer to trial this. I suggest really using the app before deciding to purchase, as I think it’s overpriced for what it offers and the app feels like it’s in beta mode tbh.
